card werk-test-runner-parallel  [open]
The unit tests run on parallel workers, with a per-test time limit that allows for the shared load
why: Run in one process, the unit tests take most of the time that the build loop gives one check, so a slow machine fails the check for time alone. Parallel workers make the run shorter. But the workers compete for the machine, so a test that starts many processes in sequence runs past a short per-test limit.

To keep the unit test run well inside the time limit of one check, the test command runs the test files on four worker processes at the same time. Each test gets a default limit of 15 seconds, not the runner default of 5 seconds. A test that needs more still sets its own, longer limit.

The longer limit does not hide a slow test or a frozen test. A test that hangs still fails, only 10 seconds later. A check that runs past its own time limit is a fail of the check infrastructure, not of the code (#ms-fail-cause), so the run time of the whole suite is the number to protect.

  -> depends_on      lp-checks  A check is one command and its exit code
       why: The unit test run is one check: one command whose exit code is the verdict.
  -> refines         werk-test-runner  One test runner, or one per side
  -> depends_on      ms-fail-cause  A rerun of the red check sets the flaky cause. The next builder pass sets the other causes
       why: A check that runs past its time limit fails as check infrastructure, not as code. That is the fail this card keeps the test run away from.
  <- alternative_to  werk-test-runner-parallel:opt0  Run the test files in one process, with the runner default per-test limit
Options
  werk-test-runner-parallel:opt0  Run the test files in one process, with the runner default per-test limit
    why not: The run in one process takes most of the time limit of one check. A slower machine or a few more tests then fail the check for time alone, with no fault in the code.
-----
card werk-test-dom  [decided]
Component tests share one DOM for the whole unit run
why: Server tests and React component tests run in one process and need different globals, and React finds a DOM only if one exists when it first loads.

This is the way werk meets #werk-test-globals. One DOM window is registered before any test file loads, so React finds a DOM when it first loads. The network, stream and timer globals of the runtime are put back after the registration, so a server test in the same run uses the real network function, not the one of the DOM. Each component test unmounts what it rendered.

The test runner and the client framework that this rests on are chosen in #werk-test-runner.

  -> refines         werk-stack  werk's client is built from components on one framework
  -> depends_on      werk-test-globals  Each test runs with the globals that its own code expects
       why: The single shared DOM is the way werk meets the rule that each test sees its own globals.
  -> depends_on      werk-test-runner  One test runner, or one per side
       why: The DOM is registered for the bun test runner that #werk-test-runner chooses, with React from the same card.
  <- alternative_to  werk-test-dom:opt0  Register a DOM per component test file and remove it after the file
  <- refines         werk-test-dom:opt0  Register a DOM per component test file and remove it after the file
Options
  werk-test-dom:opt0  Register a DOM per component test file and remove it after the file
    why not: React finds a DOM only when it first loads in the process. A DOM registered later, or removed and registered again for each file, is not the one React already holds, so only the first file would be safe. The shared DOM also costs one registration, not one per file.

/**
 * The unit test preload (#werk-test-env). It runs once, before the first test.
 *
 * It replaces the environment of the run with a clean one: no variable that points at a real
 * project, a fresh home folder, and the fake agent first on PATH. Bun's process spawn and
 * program lookup read the environment that the process started with, not process.env as it
 * is now, so the preload also makes them default to the clean environment. The shell and
 * node:child_process already read process.env.
 *
 * After each test, it ends the test's scope: it stops the servers and removes the projects
 * that the test started, also when the test fails.
 */
import { afterEach } from 'bun:test'
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { cleanEnv } from './clean-env.ts'
import { writeFakeAgent } from './fake-bin.ts'
import { endTestScope } from './harness.ts'

const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'werk-test-run-'))
const fakeBin = join(root, 'bin')
const home = join(root, 'home')
writeFakeAgent(fakeBin)
mkdirSync(home)

const clean = cleanEnv(process.env, { fakeBin, home, agentScript: join(root, 'agent-script.json') })
for (const key of Object.keys(process.env)) if (!(key in clean)) delete process.env[key]
Object.assign(process.env, clean)

type SpawnOptions = { env?: Record<string, string | undefined> } | undefined

/** The options with the clean environment as the default, read at the moment of the spawn. */
const withEnv = <T extends SpawnOptions>(options: T): T => (options?.env ? options : ({ ...options, env: { ...process.env } } as T))

const { spawn, spawnSync, which } = Bun
// Bun.spawn takes the command first and the options second, or one object that holds both.
Bun.spawn = ((cmdOrOptions: unknown, options?: SpawnOptions) =>
  Array.isArray(cmdOrOptions)
    ? spawn(cmdOrOptions, withEnv(options) as never)
    : spawn(withEnv(cmdOrOptions as SpawnOptions) as never)) as typeof Bun.spawn
Bun.spawnSync = ((cmdOrOptions: unknown, options?: SpawnOptions) =>
  Array.isArray(cmdOrOptions)
    ? spawnSync(cmdOrOptions, withEnv(options) as never)
    : spawnSync(withEnv(cmdOrOptions as SpawnOptions) as never)) as typeof Bun.spawnSync
Bun.which = ((command: string, options?: { PATH?: string; cwd?: string }) =>
  which(command, { PATH: process.env.PATH, ...options })) as typeof Bun.which
Bun.$.env(process.env)

afterEach(endTestScope)
---

The staged change on `#werk-test-dom` now says the rule holds for any number of test processes. It waits for your ✓.

1. **Title:** "Component tests share one DOM in each test process". The words "the whole unit run" no longer appear.
2. **Defined term:** a test process is one running copy of the test runner. All test files in that process share its globals.
3. **New paragraph:** a parallel run (`#werk-test-runner-parallel`) has one test process per worker. Each worker registers its own DOM in the same way. No DOM is shared between workers, and none needs to be, because each test file runs inside one worker only.
4. **Why:** now ends with "however many processes the run uses".

The rejected option on the card ("Register a DOM per component test file") already says "in the process", so it needs no change.
